Section 1: Company Overview & Audited Financial Baseline

JD.com, Inc. (converted at an exchange rate of RMB 6.9931 / $1.00 USD; 1 ADS = 2 Class A Ordinary Shares) operates the largest first-party (1P) supply-chain-driven merchandise and logistics ecosystem in Greater China. Unlike pure-play asset-light digital matchmakers that operate strictly as marketplace tollbooths, JD functions as a vertically integrated commercial enterprise that marries direct retail inventory procurement with an owned nationwide fulfillment network. The economic engine converts massive purchasing volume into low-cost procurement, passes structural scale savings back to consumers through guaranteed product authenticity and rapid delivery (the "211" same-day/next-day standard), and monetizes logistics, advertising, and supply chain technology services across third-party (3P) merchants and external enterprises.

The core business disaggregates into three distinct operating divisions:

  • JD Retail (85.2% of Net Revenues): Comprises direct 1P sales and the 3P merchant marketplace across two primary product categories. Electronics and Home Appliances remains the bedrock cash-generation anchor ($22.58 billion / RMB 157.9B in Q2 2026), though near-term performance reflects macroeconomic headwinds and high comparison bases from 2025 government trade-in subsidies (-11.8% YoY in Q2 2026). General Merchandise (supermarket FMCG, healthcare via JD Health, apparel, and home goods) reached $15.62 billion / RMB 109.2B in Q2 2026 (+5.6% YoY), providing higher-frequency consumer touchpoints. JD Retail delivered an operating margin of 4.6% in Q2 2026 ($1.93 billion / RMB 13.47B operating profit), demonstrating pricing discipline amidst aggressive domestic competitor subsidies.
  • JD Logistics (JDL) (12.2% of Net Revenues): Operates over 1,600 warehouses spanning more than 34 million square meters of logistics real estate, including 45 automated "Asia No. 1" smart fulfillment mega-hubs. External customer revenue grew 24.3% YoY in Q2 2026 to RMB 64.10 billion, now representing over 70% of total JDL revenue. Integration of Deppon express freight and expanding overseas fulfillment centers (>200 facilities spanning >1.3M sqm across Western Europe and the Middle East) have established stable segment operating margins in the 2.5% to 3.5% range.
  • New Businesses (2.6% of Net Revenues): Encompasses Joybuy / JoyExpress (European omni-channel B2C retail and logistics infrastructure), local on-demand retail, and food delivery pilots. Segment operating losses spiked to RMB 47.03B ($6.72B) in FY2025 due to initial market entry subsidies, but narrowed sharply to RMB 9.85B in Q2 2026 following aggressive promotional rationalization and integration into JDL's delivery network.

The company monitors operational health through four primary performance metrics: (1) Annual Active Customer Accounts exceeding 700 million with quarterly shopping frequency compounding above 40% year-over-year; (2) Inventory Turnover Efficiency maintained at approximately 30.2 to 31.5 days across millions of stock-keeping units (SKUs); (3) Fulfillment Expense Ratio optimized at 7.1% of net revenues; and (4) Services & Advertising Revenue Mix expanding to 10.4% of product revenues ($4.42 billion / RMB 30.9B in Q2 2026, +8.3% YoY), steadily expanding consolidated gross margins to 17.1% (+120 bps YoY).

Audited Cash Flow & Unlevered Owner Earnings Waterfall (LTM Q2 2026):

  1. GAAP Operating Cash Flow (Line 1): Reported trailing twelve months GAAP Operating Cash Flow stands at RMB 51.12 billion ($7.31 billion USD).
  2. Post-Tax Interest Expense Add-back (Line 2): Adding back post-tax interest expense of $0.35 billion (RMB 2.45 billion) to establish a true Unlevered Free Cash Flow to Firm (FCFF) baseline prior to balance sheet debt obligations.
  3. Non-Operating Interest Income Deduction (Line 3): Treasury interest income of $0.89 billion (RMB 6.25 billion) earned on corporate bank deposits is stripped from operating cash flows to eliminate double-counting on the balance sheet cash bridge.
  4. Capital Expenditures & Maintenance Allocation (Line 4): Total LTM additions to property, equipment, logistics facilities, and software totaled $2.82 billion (RMB 19.72 billion). Maintenance CapEx is isolated at $1.57 billion (RMB 11.00 billion) required to sustain warehouse automation clusters, delivery fleet renewals, and server infrastructure.
  5. Stock-Based Compensation Cash Charge (Line 5): Share-based compensation of $0.60 billion (RMB 4.20 billion) is deducted at 100% face value as a real economic expense to prevent shareholder dilution.
  6. Audited Core Baseline Unlevered Owner Earnings (OE₀): $7.31B (GAAP OCF) + $0.35B (Interest Addback) - $0.89B (Interest Income) - $1.57B (Maintenance CapEx) - $0.60B (100% SBC) = $4.30 Billion USD ($3.30 per diluted ADS across 1,302 million diluted ADSs). Pre-SBC Unlevered FCFF baseline stands at $4.90 Billion USD ($3.76 per ADS).

Balance Sheet Fortress & Unencumbered Net Cash Bridge (as of June 30, 2026):

  • Gross Cash, Restricted Cash & Short-Term Marketable Investments: RMB 235.10 billion ($33.62 billion USD).
  • Funded Debt Deductions: Deducting short-term borrowings of $1.15 billion (RMB 8.01 billion) and long-term unsecured senior notes/loans of $5.96 billion (RMB 41.69 billion), total $7.11 billion.
  • Lease Liabilities & Repatriation Friction: Deducting non-cancelable ASC 842 operating lease commitments ($2.50 billion) and a conservative 7.0% cross-border dividend withholding tax friction ($1.50 billion) on onshore cash reserves.
  • Strategic Equity Holdings Bridge: Crediting unconsolidated strategic equity stakes (including JD Technology, Dada Nexus, Deppon, and Kuayue Express) valued conservatively at $2.67 billion (RMB 18.67 billion) after applying a standard 25.0% illiquidity/holding-company haircut.
  • Surplus Net Cash & Strategic Value Floor: $33.62B (Cash) - $7.11B (Debt) - $2.50B (Leases) - $1.50B (Tax Friction) + $2.67B (Affiliates) = $25.18 Billion USD (+$19.34 per ADS across 1,302M diluted ADSs).

Executive Leadership Commentary & 4-Quarter Trajectory

Sandy Xu, Chief Executive Officer: "We navigated the first half of 2026 by deepening our operational core. We continued to see robust user growth and increased shopping frequency, with annual active customers surpassing 700 million. Our core JD Retail business remained resilient, expanding gross margins to 18.5% and preserving operating margins at 4.6% despite intense domestic price competition. Our low-price strategy is driven strictly by supply chain efficiencies and structural cost advantages, not unsustainable artificial subsidies. Furthermore, our international logistics backbone in Europe and JoyExpress are proving that our core supply chain capabilities are exportable across global markets."

Ian Su Shan, Chief Financial Officer: "Our financial framework balances disciplined capital allocation with aggressive shareholder returns. In the first half of 2026 alone, we returned $1.0 billion via share repurchases under our $5.0 billion authorization, retiring 2.5% of our share count (34 million ADSs), alongside our regular annual cash dividend of $1.00 per ADS ($1.3 billion total payout). Our investments in local on-demand retail have rationalized rapidly, while JD Logistics and 3P marketplace advertising are generating steady cash flows that drove trailing twelve months free cash flow to RMB 31.4 billion."

Section 2: The Three Forward-Looking Operating Stories

Story 1: Bear Case — Structural Hardlines Stagnation & Persisting Subsidy Drain

Under this conservative narrative, China’s macroeconomic real estate recovery remains subdued, suppressing replacement cycles for big-ticket electronics and home appliances (-2.0% annual CAGR in 1P hardlines over 5 years). PDD Holdings and Alibaba continue aggressive pricing pressure, constraining JD Retail's 3P marketplace take-rates and forcing elevated marketing spend to maintain user scale. Concurrently, New Businesses food delivery and local on-demand retail subsidies remain an ongoing cash drag, absorbing RMB 12.0B to RMB 15.0B annually. Group gross margin remains capped at 16.5%, and consolidated operating margins compress to 2.5%. Unlevered Owner Earnings decline at a -2.0% CAGR for 5 years, converting to a terminal growth rate of 1.0% under an 11.5% hurdle rate.

Story 2: Base Case — Supply Chain Scale Economies & 3P High-Margin Monetization

Under the baseline thesis, core 1P Electronics stabilizes (+2.5% CAGR) as replacement cycles normalize, while General Merchandise (FMCG, healthcare, apparel) expands at a 6.0% CAGR. The primary economic growth engine shifts toward high-margin 3P Marketplace and Marketing Services (+8.5% CAGR), driven by over 50,000 merchants deploying JD's ChatRhino AI automated hosts. JD Logistics scales external corporate fulfillment contracts (+15.0% CAGR), expanding JDL segment operating margins to 3.5%. New Businesses losses narrow systematically to breakeven by Year 3 through food delivery subsidy rationalization. Consolidated gross margin expands to 18.2%, pushing group operating margin to 4.5%. Unlevered Owner Earnings compound at a 6.0% CAGR for 5 years, with a 2.5% terminal growth rate discounted at 10.0%.

Story 3: Bull Case — JDL Network Externalization & Global AI Smart Supply Chain

In the optimistic expansion scenario, domestic discretionary spending rebounds sharply (+5.0% 1P hardlines CAGR). 3P marketplace revenue accelerates (+14.0% CAGR) as merchant adoption of JD's on-demand retail infrastructure expands rapidly. JD Logistics fully realizes operating leverage from its 34M+ sqm domestic network and European automated fulfillment hubs, capturing high-margin international logistics contracts and expanding JDL operating margins to 5.0%. AI-driven supply chain automation lowers fulfillment expense ratios to 6.2% of revenue. New Businesses pivot into a high-margin logistics platform, achieving group operating margins of 6.0%. Unlevered Owner Earnings compound at a 12.0% CAGR for 5 years, entering a 3.0% terminal growth regime discounted at 9.5%.

Section 3: Valuation Across the 3 Stories

The consolidated DCF valuation incorporates our audited unlevered Owner Earnings baseline ($4.30B post-full SBC charge / $3.30 per ADS across 1,302M ADSs) and adds back unencumbered surplus net cash and strategic affiliate equity value ($19.34 per ADS) to establish the intrinsic value per ADS across all three scenarios.
